entry.title: SAP DM Manage Next Numbers Extension – “Failed to create identifier” before REST endpoint is called
entry.content:
We are trying to use a custom Next Number Extension in SAP Digital Manufacturing to set the SFC identifier based on the production order number. 

We are aware that the standard Manage Next Numbers configuration can use replaceable parameters such as {ORDER_NAME} in the prefix. For example, this allows the generated SFC to start with the production order number. However, SAP DM still automatically appends the sequence value based on Current Sequence / Increment By, resulting in values such as 35258491, 35258492, etc. In our case, we do not want any additional sequence suffix. For non-serialized orders where the whole order should be represented by a single SFC, the desired result is simply SFC = ORDER_NAME.

The custom Next Number extension is implemented in SAP Integration Suite as an iFlow exposing a REST endpoint. The extension is also registered in Manage Service Registry as:

  • Type: HTTP
  • Protocol: REST
  • Method: POST
  • Is Extension: Yes
  • Endpoint points to an SAP Integration Suite iFlow
  • Web Server and CPI_DESTINATION_IFLMAP are configured with OAuth2ClientCredentials

In Manage Next Numbers we use:

  • Source: Local
  • Extension: our custom service
  • Extension Destination: CPI_DESTINATION_IFLMAP

The same registered service/iFlow can be called successfully from a Production Process Design (PPD), so the endpoint and authentication are working.
However, when the extension is used during SFC Release, SAP DM returns:

Failed to create identifier
shopOrder.release.createIdentifiers.error
HTTP 400

The main issue is that no request reaches the Integration Suite iFlow at all when triggered from Manage Next Numbers.

Has anyone successfully used a Next Number Extension with an SAP Integration Suite endpoint?
Are there any additional requirements for the Service Registry definition or Extension Destination specifically for Manage Next Numbers?
Thanks!

entry.title: SAP API Management - Unable to rewrite backend target URL/path dynamically
entry.content:
I am facing an issue in SAP Integration Suite - API Management regarding backend URL rewriting before the request is sent to the target endpoint.

My public endpoint:

GET /gestaopessoas/funcionarios/cpf?matricula=10071015

Backend that should be called:

https://<host>/http/ura/cpfconsultation?matricula=10071015

Instead, SAP APIM always calls:

https://<host>/http/funcionarios/cpf?matricula=10071015

My Environment

  • SAP Integration Suite
  • SAP API Management
  • API Proxy created manually (not generated from OpenAPI)
  • Target Endpoint type: URL (not API Provider)
  • OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials implemented successfully using:
    • KVM
    • BasicAuthentication
    • ServiceCallout
    • ExtractVariables
    • AssignMessage

The OAuth flow is working correctly.

The only remaining issue is rewriting the backend URL/path.

What we already tested

We tested several approaches.

JavaScript

We successfully executed JavaScript inside the ProxyEndpoint Flow.

We changed:

context.setVariable("target.url", "...");

context.setVariable("request.path", "...");

context.setVariable("dynamic.target", "...");

context.setVariable("target.copy.pathsuffix", false);

The Trace confirms that all variables are correctly updated.

Example:

dynamic.target =
https://<host>/http/ura/cpfconsultation?matricula=10071015

and

target.copy.pathsuffix = false

However, in the final execution step SAP API Management ignores all these values.

The final Trace always shows:

target.url =
https://<host>/http

request.uri =
/http/funcionarios/cpf

request.path =
/http/funcionarios/cpf

which means the runtime rebuilds the backend URL before sending the request.

AssignMessage

We also tried using AssignMessage to modify:

  • Path
  • request.path
  • target.url

However either:

  • the policy XML is rejected by the parser, or
  • the runtime ignores the modifications.

ServiceCallout

ServiceCallout is working correctly.

It successfully obtains an OAuth token from the OAuth Authorization Server.

Therefore the issue is unrelated to OAuth.

Expected behavior

We expect SAP API Management to allow rewriting the backend URI before sending the request.

For example:

Public URI

/funcionarios/cpf

should become

/ura/cpfconsultation

without changing the public API exposed to consumers.
In my opinion this is a common API Gateway feature.

Question
Could you please clarify:

  1. Is backend path rewriting supported in SAP API Management?
  2. Is there any supported policy or configuration to rewrite the backend URI before sending the request?
  3. Is modifying target.url, request.path, dynamic.target or target.copy.pathsuffix supported?
  4. Is this behavior expected when using URL Target Endpoints?
  5. If backend URI rewriting is supported, could you provide the recommended approach?

entry.title: SAP CPI dateTrans Function Returning Incorrect Date During Conversion
entry.content:
We are using the dateTrans function in SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) to convert a datetime value from the format:

yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss

to:

yyyy-MM-dd

However, the dateTrans function is producing an incorrect output.

Input

2026-10-07 18:15:00

Expected Output

2026-10-07

Actual Output

2027-03-07

The input date is being converted to a completely different date, even though the expected behavior is only to remove the time portion and retain the date.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create a mapping in SAP Cloud Integration.
  2. Use the dateTrans function for date conversion.
  3. Provide the input value:

2026-10-07 18:15:00

  1. Configure the conversion from:

yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss to: yyyy-MM-dd

entry.title: SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) - CSRF Token Invalid (/IWBEP/CM_V4H_RUN/042)
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I am trying to call an ABAP OData V4 service from SAP Cloud Integration using the HTTP Adapter.

Scenario

I need to perform a POST operation against the following OData V4 service.

The same flow works successfully in Postman but fails from CPI with:

GET call postman

 

 
 
POST call postman

 

JSON
 
{
 
"error": {
 
"code": "/IWBEP/CM_V4H_RUN/042",
 
"message": "CSRF token is invalid",
 
"@SAP__common.ExceptionCategory": "CSRF_Token_Missing"
 
}
 
}

Current iFlow

Plain Text
 
Content Modifier 1
 
|--> x-csrf-token = Fetch
 
Request Reply (GET)
 
Content Modifier 2
 
|
 
Groovy Script
 
 
 
Request Reply (POST)

GET Call

Header:

 
 
 
HTTP
 
x-csrf-token: Fetch
 
``

HTTP Adapter Configuration:

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
Method: GET
 
Request Headers: x-csrf-token
 
Response Headers: *

The GET response returns:

 
 
 
HTTP
 
x-csrf-token: <token>
 
set-cookie:
 
sap-usercontext=...
 
sap-XSRF_AST_367=...

My Understanding

Postman works because:

  1. GET with:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: Fetch

  2. Receives:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: <real token>
     
    Set-Cookie: ...

  3. POST is executed with:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: <real token>
     
    Cookie: ...

and Postman automatically maintains the HTTP session.

CPI Implementation

I found a blog/forum example suggesting: https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-q-a/calling-an-odata-v4-custom-action-from-within-an-iflow/qaq-p/14088969 

Groovy

 
Groovy
 
import com.sap.gateway.ip.core.customdev.util.Message
 
 
 
def Message processData(Message message) {
 
 
 
def headers = message.getHeaders()
 
 
 
message.setProperty("CsrfToken",
 
headers.get("x-csrf-token"))
 
 
 
message.setProperty("CookieHeader",
 
headers.get("set-cookie"))
 
return message
 
}

Content Modifier before POST

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
 
 
 
Header Name Source Type Source Value
 
------------------------------------------------
 
x-csrf-token Property CsrfToken
 
Cookie Property CookieHeader

POST HTTP Adapter

Request Headers:

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
x-csrf-token|Cookie

Question

  1. Is this the correct approach for manually handling CSRF tokens in CPI HTTP Adapter?

  2. Is it mandatory to pass the cookies returned in set-cookie as a request header named Cookie for ABAP OData V4 services?

  3. Has anyone successfully implemented GET (Fetch CSRF) + POST using HTTP Adapter against an ABAP OData V4 endpoint?

  4. Is there a better CPI-native way to preserve the HTTP session between the GET and POST calls?

Any guidance or working example would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance!

entry.title: Avoiding Order Lock Conflicts in S/4HANA During Concurrent Updates from CPI
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I would like to seek your advice on handling order lock conflicts in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud during updates from SAP CPI.

Our scenario is as follows:

  • An external system sends multiple messages for the same order in separate transactions.
  • SAP CPI processes each message independently and updates the corresponding order in S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  • While the first message is still processing and updating the order, a second message for the same order arrives and attempts another update.
  • Since the order is still being processed by the first transaction, it is locked in S/4HANA Public Cloud, causing the second message to fail with a lock-related error.

Has anyone encountered a similar situation? What approaches or best practices would you recommend to prevent or handle these order lock conflicts?

For example:

  • Is there a way to queue or serialize updates for the same order?
  • Are there standard SAP patterns for managing concurrent updates to the same business object?

Any guidance or recommendations would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

#sapcpi #sapintegrationsuite

I am trying to access SAP Integration Suite in my personal SAP BTP Trial account, but I am redirected to an unauthorized page.

Environment:
- SAP BTP Trial account
- Region: US10 (AWS)
- SAP Integration Suite plan: trial
- Subscription status: Subscribed
- Identity Provider: Default Identity Provider

I would appreciate any advice.

Thank you for your help.
